summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq old houses/14)

data.turoyo: Ánnaqqa hano, mǝd yaqəḏ ṭowo, bəṯr me šabṯo dǧuġrile, kḥawri ak+kefe, kxayfi, kowən xayife. Dəmmina, i+kefo ḥamši kilowatyo, kfayšo ʕaṣro+kilowat, lo?
data.translation: Now then, this one, once it has burnt well, after they have been heating it for a week, the stones blanch, they get light, they become light. So to speak, a stone is fifty kilos, it preserves ten kilos, right?

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; physical weight loss during calcination is quantified in the following sentence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Ishaq old houses/14)

data.turoyo: Ánnaqqa hano, mǝd yaqəḏ ṭowo, bəṯr me šabṯo dǧuġrile, kḥawri ak+kefe, kxayfi, kowən xayife. Dəmmina, i+kefo ḥamši kilowatyo, kfayšo ʕaṣro+kilowat, lo?

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (JTM 5.5/6)

data.turoyo: u zʕuro mədle w rahoṭo… gədəmmət balki ʕal u pəskilet kuzze, hawxa xayifo kuzze.
data.translation: Der Junge nahm (das Geld) und im Laufschritt ... du hättest meinen können, er führe auf dem Fahrrad, so schnell lief er los.

rationale: New speed sense; running and bicycle comparison provide independent Turoyo support.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (LuF 3/3)

data.turoyo: Karrakore, yaʕni smiṯo w lə kšəmʕo, haṯe kuyo kriṯo ḥləmto w latyo xayəfto ġalabe bu rahṭo.
data.translation: "Karrakore" bedeutet: (sie ist) blind und hört nicht. Das ist eine kurze, gedrungene (Schlange), nicht sehr rasch in der Fortbewegung (wörtl.: im Lauf).

rationale: New speed sense; feminine xayəfto with explicit domain bu rahṭo.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (PrS 74/65)

data.turoyo: Gamlo, kle u malaxo, dray ṣlibo l foṯəx w ʕaməṣ ʕaynəx, xayifo d šoqəl ruḥəx. Elo mʕawaqlan u malaxo, gəmqatəl Mšiḥo aʕme.
data.translation: Kamel, da ist der Engel, schlag ein Kreuz über dein Gesicht und schliesse die Augen; er hat's eilig, deine Seele zu holen, aber wir haben ihn aufgehalten, der Messias wird mit ihm zanken.

rationale: Speed/haste as a predicate with d-action complement, rather than only an adverb.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (29/164)

data.turoyo: Hano farəs yo, xayifo yo. Latyo, xəd Ḥasan, b ʕumro rabo.
data.translation: Dies ist ein guter Reiter, und er ist schnell. Er ist auch nicht so alt wie Hasan.

rationale: New speed sense; adjective predicate of a rider with yo, not a change-of-state event.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (62/229)

data.turoyo: Ḥzeli ʕayno d maye, amma xayifo maye lə kṯe mina, anǧax saʕaye gməmloyo ṭaṣe d maye d šotat
data.translation: Ich habe eine Wasserquelle gefunden; aber schnell kommt das Wasser nicht aus ihr heraus. Erst in einer Stunde wird sich eine Schale mit Wasser füllen, so daß du trinken kannst.

rationale: Fifth speed example; slow filling independently establishes rate, with invariant adverb modifying water flow.

summary: example for sense 3 in Part act. (62/208)

data.turoyo: U malko omər: “Abro! Mə xayifo aṯət! Fayšatwa hul ṣafro! Mu sabab balki məǧġolowa aʕmux m iḏe d ṣafro?”
data.translation: Der König sprach: "Mein Sohn! Was bist du so früh gekommen? Wärest du doch bis zum Morgen geblieben! Vielleicht hätte sie beim Anbruch des Morgens mit dir gesprochen!"

rationale: Temporal sense independently supported by the contrast with staying until morning; adds to the two existing temporal examples.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/993)

data.turoyo: B dukṯe u swedi yo, u ingilizi yo. Bəṯər i bagiye w i šexane, am mədonani ste gədxayfi, lə gədfayši ġalabe.
data.translation: In its place is Swedish, English. Then the bagiye and the shekhane, these things too will become fewer; they will not remain much.

rationale: Thin Infectum1 and cultural-frequency subject; following negative 'remain much' confirms attenuation. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
rationale: Explicitly includes the literal light-weight state shown by xayife after kowən, alongside the existing change of weight.

summary: Qaṭəl xayəf / feminine xayifo in Preterit Intransitive describes becoming lighter, whereas xayifo / feminine xayəfto in the existing Part act. convention can predicate a state or modify an action. Copulas, agreement and context matter more than identical spelling.

Physical weight remains sense 1; illness severity and difficulty of a situation (existing 24/80, 78/180) remain contextual extensions of lightening/easing. No separate participant-based senses are added.

The speed sense occurs as a property of human or animal movement, a haste predicate with d-, and an invariant manner/rate modifier. The strongest contexts establish speed in Turoyo independently of translation.
Part act. is retained following the entry's own filing of these adjectives and adverbial forms. Whether synchronically verbal or lexicalised remains a question, not a new form claim.

Several speed proposals are ambiguous in isolation (MAC Material culture/105, MAC NE Sterka Zera/6, 50/8); they are not used as publication examples. The swift-camel proposal is compatible with sense 2 but is weaker than the selected contexts.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce: the supplied English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. All semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo; quoted English is copied from the supplied machine translation.
The round-1 distinction among weight/easing1, speed2 and earliness3 is essential. Identical xayifo does not select a meaning without its predicate and context.

The physical-weakness interpretation in2.4/1065 relies heavily on machine English. Adverbial quick death is equally plausible from the supplied clause and is not used to create or illustrate a weakness sense.
Part act. filing follows the inherited adjective/adverb convention. gədxayfi is Infectum; no III token supplies the inherited missing causative base forms.
Should lexicalised xayifo/xayəfto speed and early forms remain within Part act., as the inherited entry treats comparable uses, or receive an adjective/adverb cross-reference?
At 52/122, does the original edition support früh or schnell? Preserve existing früh until the unsupplied dictionary claim can be checked.
Confirm the scope of ínaqqa d̥xayifo dlo+mənqoliwa at MAC Material culture/105 and elo xayifo at MAC NE Sterka Zera/6. At 50/8, is it quickly or early?
Does MAC old houses/14 kxayfi follow the entry's Infectum vocalism, or should it be ko-Preterit? The supplied paradigm is insufficient to decide otherwise.
The III base forms remain blank in the inherited entry; no III token in this batch permits reconstruction.
In2.4/1065 does xayifo modify dying as 'quickly', or describe the sufferer as physically weak? No example is published pending that distinction.
In4.II/993 is decline measured in frequency, number of performances or cultural prominence? The Turoyo supports attenuation, not a more precise measure.
Retain adjective/adverb xayifo in Part act. or cross-reference a lexical entry? This is the same unresolved classification issue as round 1.
Separate von dem
rationale: The German preposition and article are separate words: von dem. The supplied corpus translation reproduces the same apparent spacing typo, so it does not justify retaining vondem.

summary: Capitalize the German noun Bissen
rationale: Bissen is a German noun and requires a capital B. The supplied corpus translation also has lowercase bissen, an evident inherited capitalization error.

summary: War becoming less intense, a calmer situation, and waning prominence/frequency of named practices extend easing/lightening. No separate senses are required.
Round-1 earliness3 also predicates that drawing conclusions is premature; the temporal meaning is already proposed and is not repeated.
